# Assembly format

How a microinstruction of the ND-100, ND-110 and ND-120 is written as text.

Source: [`defs/format/assembly-format.yaml`](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/defs/format/assembly-format.yaml).

## Header of `assembly-format.yaml`

```text
ND-100/110/120 Microcode Assembly Format Rules

This file is the canonical specification for how microinstructions are
formatted as human-readable assembly text. It is consumed by:
  - The disassembler (to generate output matching hand-written .uc sources)
  - The assembler (to parse .uc sources into binary)
  - The VSCode extension (to understand line structure for folding/hover)

The format is known as the "3-line format" because each microinstruction
typically spans 3 source lines. Simple instructions may collapse to fewer.

Reference: ND-06.031.1 EN ND-110 and ND-120 Microprogrammer's Guide
Reference implementation: ND110Compile/ND110Compile/uCode/ND-110-RASK.uc
```

## Format name

ND 3-line microcode assembly

## Models

nd100, nd110, nd120

| `label_suffix` | : |
| `address_prefix_suffix` | / |
| `statement_terminator` | ; |

## Layout

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `default_lines` | 3 |

### Line 1

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Register and ALU |
| `purpose` | Select register operands and ALU operation |
| `token_categories` | AB\_REG, A\_REG, B\_REG, PIC, ALUF, ALUD, ALUM, STS, CRY, MIS, XRF |

### Line 2

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Bus and sequencing (true path) |
| `purpose` | Select IDB source, issue command, control true-path sequencing |
| `token_categories` | IDBS, COMM, T\_SEQ, T\_STK, LCOUNT |

### Line 3

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Branch or condition |
| `purpose` | Specify branch target or condition test with false-path sequencing |

#### Variants

| name | applies\_when | example | content\_order | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| branch\_only | SCOND == 0 AND CONDENABL == 0 | FTCH2:<br># ... line 1 and line 2 ...<br>PVPF; % line 3: jump to label PVPF | branch\_target |  |
| condition\_test | SCOND == 1 | COND,FETCH F,NEXT F,HOLD; | COND, F\_SEQ, F\_STK | When a condition test is active, the instruction also specifies<br>a TRUE path (T,xxx on line 2) and a FALSE path (F,xxx on line 3).<br>The CPU evaluates the condition and picks the appropriate path. |
| cond\_enable | CONDENABL == 1 | FTCH CONDENABL;<br>NOINT CONDENABL;<br>FTCH2 CONDENABL; | branch\_target, CONDENABL | CONDENABL enables conditional sequencing using a previously set<br>condition. The branch target is taken if the condition was TRUE;<br>otherwise the FALSE-path fields (from a prior instruction, or<br>implicit F,NEXT/F,HOLD) are used.<br>Typically appears PAIRED with a preceding instruction that sets<br>the condition (e.g. COND,FETCH F,NEXT F,HOLD). |

## Collapse rules

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `single_line_allowed_when` | Only line 2 has non-default fields, Branch target is short and fits |

### Examples

| source | explanation |
| --- | --- |
| T,JMP 6 COMM,SLOW1; | Simple unconditional jump to label 6 with SLOW1 command |
| T,JMP 11 COMM,SLOW1; | Jump to address 11 (octal), same pattern |
| ALUD,NONE IDBS,ALU COMM,SLOW1 T,JMP T,HOLD ILLIN; | All three lines on one physical line |

## Zero display

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `principle` | Most fields default to zero, and zero-valued fields are NOT emitted.<br>However, certain fields ARE emitted even when zero because:<br>(a) they carry semantic meaning ("explicit NOP" vs "absent")<br>(b) they appear paired with non-zero fields from another category<br>(c) Norsk Data source conventions display them unconditionally |

### Always emit zero token

| token | category | encoding\_all\_zero | reason | emit\_when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T,JMP | T\_SEQ | yes | T,JMP has zero encoding but is the default true-sequence when SCOND=1 or when a branch target is present | Any T\_SEQ/T\_STK/branch\_target is present on line 2 |
| T,HOLD | T\_STK | yes | Default true-path stack operation; always paired with T\_SEQ | Line 2 has any sequencing tokens |
| F,JMP | F\_SEQ | yes | Default false-path sequence when a condition test is active | SCOND == 1 (condition test active on line 3) |
| F,HOLD | F\_STK | yes | Default false-path stack operation; always paired with F\_SEQ when SCOND=1 | SCOND == 1 |
| ALUD,Q | ALUD | yes | Zero in ALUD field means 'F -&gt; Q', which is semantically meaningful (not a no-op) | Any ALU operation is specified on line 1 |
| IDBS,ALU | IDBS | yes | Default IDB source is the ALU output; shown when any line 2 activity exists | Line 2 has other non-default fields (COMM, T\_SEQ, etc.) |
| PIC,MCL | PIC | yes | PIC command MASTER CLEAR - zero encoding but real meaning when COMM=EPIC | COMM == EPIC |
| A,Z | A\_REG | yes | A-operand=0 addresses zero/status register; shown when needed contextually | ALU requires A-operand (ALUF uses A) OR COMM requires address |
| B,Z | B\_REG | yes | B-operand=0 addresses zero/status register | ALU requires B-operand (ALUF uses B) OR COMM requires address |

### Suppress when zero

| category | reason | exception |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ALUF | Zero means no ALU operation specified |  |
| COMM | Zero means no command issued |  |
| STS | Zero means no status update |  |
| CRY | Zero means normal carry-in (not overridden) |  |
| MIS | Zero means no shift mode modifier |  |
| ALUM | Zero means ALUM,MIC (default, only shown when different) | ALUM,MIC (the zero-encoded default) may be shown when MIS is non-zero |
| COND | Zero means no condition test |  |
| LCOUNT | Zero means loop counter not active |  |
| CONDENABL | Zero means conditional sequencing not enabled |  |

## Operand requirements

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `RequireA` | Token requires an A-operand to be specified |
| `RequireB` | Token requires a B-operand to be specified |
| `RequireA_B` | Token requires both A and B operands (AB, tokens) |
| `RequirePIC` | Token requires a PIC command on the A-operand position (COMM,EPIC must be present) |
| `IsA` | Token provides the A-operand (mutually exclusive with other A providers) |
| `IsB` | Token provides the B-operand |
| `IsA_B` | Token provides both A and B (AB, aliases) |
| `IsPIC` | Token is a PIC command (occupies A-operand slot when COMM,EPIC is active) |
| `IsIDBS` | Token sets the IDBS field |
| `IsTrueAddr` | Token sets the T\_SEQ field (T,JMP/T,NEXT/T,RETURN) |
| `IsTrueStack` | Token sets the T\_STK field (T,HOLD/T,POP/T,LOAD/T,PUSH) |
| `IsFalseAddr` | Token sets the F\_SEQ field (F,JMP/F,NEXT/F,RETURN) |
| `IsFalseStack` | Token sets the F\_STK field (F,HOLD/F,POP/F,LOAD/F,PUSH) |
| `IsCond` | Token sets the COND field (condition selector) |

## Branch targets

### Forms

| label | octal\_address | self |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Symbolic label resolved at assembly time (e.g. PVPF, FTCH2) |  |  |
|  | Plain octal number (e.g. 6, 11, 170000) |  |
|  |  | Omitted - branch to current address (implicit in some forms) |

### Address extension

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `description` | The branch address is 13 bits: CSBIT20 (bit 20) is the high bit and<br>CSBIT\_11\_0 (bits 11:0) are the low bits. Labels are resolved to a full<br>13-bit address by the assembler. |
| `effective_width` | 13 |
| `formula` | effective\_address = (CSBIT20 &lt;&lt; 12) \| CSBIT\_11\_0 |

## Special tokens

| Key | category | bit | appears\_on | always\_displayed | description | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CONDENABL` | special | 23 | line\_3 | yes | Enables conditional sequencing based on a prior COND test |  |
| `LCOUNT` | special | 22 | line\_2 | yes | Count loop counter; if false, return and hold |  |
| `XRF` | special | 50 | line\_1 | yes | Select extended register file |  |
| `CONT` | special |  | line\_3 |  | Continue label - commonly jumped to after conditional tests | Not a special bit; just a conventional label |
